transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

I came in because I feel like my mind just won’t stop jumping between worries. One minute I’m worried our lab’s new partnership is going to mean my position gets cut, then I’m worried my data are wrong, or my bills are going to pile up, or my family thinks I’m falling behind. And then I start thinking I’ve already ruined my chances at grad school. It’s just constant.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, like restlessness, feeling on edge, muscle tension, or trouble sleeping, that seem to go along with these worries?

Yeah. At work especially, I feel really wound up, like I can’t just sit still in my chair. I’ll be tapping my foot or checking my messages over and over, or getting up and walking back to the instrument room even when I don’t really need to. And normal lab noises make me jump more than they should.

Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on quickly, maybe with symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, trembling, or feeling like you can’t breathe?

I don’t think so. I get really anxious and worked up, but I can’t say I’ve had sudden attacks like that where it hits all at once and I can’t breathe or something. It’s more like the worry is just there and keeps building.

Have you ever experienced a sudden episode where you felt intense fear or discomfort that came on quickly, maybe with symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, trembling, or feeling like you couldn’t breathe?
Not really, no. I mean, I get anxious a lot, but I haven’t had something that suddenly comes on like an attack with my heart racing or not being able to breathe.
Have you ever felt down or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, even for a period of a couple of weeks or more?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve had a stretch like that where I felt clearly depressed or stopped enjoying things for weeks. I’ve been stressed and anxious, but not really like... losing interest in everything.
Have you ever had a period where you felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, or lost interest in most things for at least two weeks in a row?
No, I don’t think I’ve had that. I mean, I have bad days, but I haven’t noticed a two-week stretch where I felt hopeless most of the day or stopped caring about most things.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or lacking energy, even when you’re not physically exhausted?

Yeah. Even if I’ve been in bed all night, I’ll wake up feeling like I barely slept, like I already pulled an all-nighter. And then during the day, even basic stuff like labeling samples at work or trying to make dinner, my body feels heavy and my brain just feels drained.
Have you had any two-week period where you felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, or stopped enjoying most things you usually like doing?

I don’t think so. I know we’ve kind of gone over that, but I haven’t had a clear two-week period where I was down or hopeless most of the day, or not enjoying most things. It’s more that I get stressed and worn out, but not like that.
Have you had any period lasting at least two weeks where you felt down or hopeless most days, or stopped enjoying most of the things you usually like to do?
No, I still wouldn’t say that. I’ve had rough stretches, but not two weeks where I felt down or hopeless most days, and I don’t think I’ve stopped enjoying most things like that.
